item.title: Congrats to Yuhang and others!
item.description: Meng, Y., Chen, F., Lu, Y., Wang, L., Yi, K., Jia, X., & Yuan, Y. (2026). Alternative splicing as an evolvable regulatory layer in plant adaptation and evolution. Horticulture Research, uhag453. https://doi.org/10.1093/hr/uhag453 Title: Alternative splicing as an evolvable regulatory layer in plant adaptation and evolution Authors: Meng, Y., Chen, F., Lu, Y., Wang, L., Yi, K., Jia, X., & Yuan, Y. Abstract: Alternative splicing (AS) is a pervasive post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism that expands transcriptomic and proteomic diversity by generating multiple isoforms from a single gene.

item.title: Congrats to Yao and others!
item.description: Lu, Y., Li, J., Yi, K., & Jia, X. (2026). Programmable plant nutrition through synthetic transportome engineering. Journal of Plant Physiology, 326, 154874. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jplph.2026.154874 Title: Programmable plant nutrition through synthetic transportome engineering Authors: Yao Lu, Jia Li, Keke Yi, Xianqing Jia Abstract: Plant nutrient homeostasis emerges from the coordinated transport, partitioning, and storage of nutrients across cellular compartments, tissues, and developmental stages. These processes form an interconnected transport system in which local changes in nutrient uptake, redistribution, or sequestration can propagate across biological scales and ultimately shape whole-plant nutrient status and growth.
